title: Akashic Delete
text: “No, just now it was trying to force me to drink its blood! All I have to do is refuse that!”
“Right! Let’s finish it off quick!”
The reincarnator turned its gaze toward me and Filolial-sama.
“Let’s manipulate that one and use it.”

The reincarnator began casting some kind of spell, indeed. Letters rose up and came flying toward us. The way these letters flew—I recognized it from past memories, thanks to Hou-kun’s blessing, as the same technique the Crimson Swine had used when it killed me.
“Taking a hostage again… you filthy lot. Akashic Delete.”

When Ark spread his hands, the enemies’ combined attack materialized into something like a book, which opened before him. Then Ark scraped away a single line of that book with his claw. Was this some kind of counterattack that used the enemy’s own gathered power against them, through coordination? Then… the reincarnator who had been trying to do something to me simply vanished. Had it not been for Hou-kun’s blessing, I doubt I could have even perceived what had happened. This state must have been equal to, or even greater than, the blessing Father had granted us during our final battle against the Crimson Swine’s true body.
“—! Wait, why? The one who was standing there—I can’t remember the name!”
“It got erased!?”

“You tried to take Motoyasu-kun hostage. That’s what you were about to do a second ago, isn’t it? You love tampering with structural information, don’t you? I could’ve done this without you noticing at all, but I let you perceive it on purpose—you get that much, right?”
Right? Ark said, tilting his head with a sharp glint in his eyes as he provoked the reincarnators.
“Well, I could erase the fact that it ever existed at all, completely—but that’s for later.”
“Maybe you should ease up a bit? If you go too far, an overprotective guardian might come running.”
Ark’s ears twitched. Was this someone he wasn’t fond of? It seemed using this kind of power tended to summon them.
“Ugh… it’s fine. They shouldn’t notice.”
“I wonder about that.”

He had seemed angry, but had he calmed down just a little? Ark traced his finger again, and the vanished letters returned. The reincarnator who had disappeared with a snap was restored just like that.
“Ah!? W-what’s going on!?”
“Understand now that rewriting backfires? Well, I won’t let you use it here anymore anyway.”
Ark slashed the reincarnators with his claw, which rose up like Spear 0’s claw, cutting through them in a single stroke. Something inside the reincarnators shattered with a crack.
“M-my ability’s—aaaaargh!? It’s gone!?”
“Don’t screw with me! Give back my cheat ability!”
“Is shouting and throwing a tantrum all you’ve got left? You’ve piled up years for nothing and turned into babies—it’s unsightly.”
“Guh…”
“Come on now, we’re not done yet.”
Ark went on slashing at the reincarnators with his claws, shred by shred, as if tormenting them.
“Ahh!? My ability—it keeps disappearing more and more!?”
“S-stop! Stop it! If this goes away—”
“Seems like all you are is some dark-souled loser acting tough thanks to your ability. Once the ability’s gone, this is what’s left—no different from a common thug or a shut-in, really.”
“You lot, who’ve done nothing but steal from others endlessly, dare say that to me? Did you ever listen to the voices of those who begged for their lives just the same?”
Ark answered with a cruel smile.
“N-no matter how much you erase, your direct attacks don’t hurt me one bit!”
“The Sacred Weapon has the power to grant countless abilities! Something this trivial, I’ll take back in no time!”
Sensing their disadvantage, the tantrum-throwing reincarnators stepped back a few paces while raising their hands toward their weapons.
“You think I’d let you run in this situation?”
Ark muttered that as he took a step forward.

“Well, even if you flee to another world, I doubt you’d get away clean. To begin with, there’s a barrier here set up by Naofumi-kun and the others. His barrier is on a completely different level from the rest, you know? Fundamentally, you two aren’t escaping.”

Ah, right—the barrier Father had set up. Now that I thought of it, Father had mentioned installing a barrier that people like the Crimson Swine’s true body couldn’t interfere with, so that a Wave-like incident would never happen again. A completely different level… just how immense must Father’s defensive ability be now, enhanced to a level rivaling Ark and Hou-kun?

“Well, since this is only about restraining the Sacred Weapon, the cat’s getting off this light—if it had gone the other way, I might’ve been driven to make things far more painful. In that sense, I suppose this is still the milder option.”
“Bhuii!”
“Hey! Isn’t there something we can do!? At this rate we’ll lose! And if that happens, we’re—our scheme will get exposed and we’re finished!”
“You said you could pull off something this big, so what the hell is this!? There’s still a way, right?”
The pig and the reincarnator’s male companion voiced their complaints at the reincarnators.
“A-ah, yeah! It’s still fine! If we work together with you two, this is an opponent we can handle!”

“Those two have rules. If we exploit the loopholes in those rules, we should be able to win! Whatever you do, don’t take the attack that grants the cat’s power! As long as we don’t drink that blood orb, we should be fine!”

“You’re cunning enough, but it looks like you don’t understand the difference between me and the cat’s rules. You probably think if you just avoid the blessing, the cat becomes powerless. Having your abilities thoroughly erased and still thinking you can win—that’s the height of ignorance.”
“If you two intend to die here by your own hand, we won’t pursue this any further.”
It wasn’t the arrogant tone that came from a dragon’s pride—it was, quite literally, an irritated and provocative tone.

“Still though… when you peek into their motives without holding back, it’s pretty shallow, huh… ‘Becoming the strongest immortal being’ seems to be the gist of it. They really love being the strongest, these two.”
“Well, scum like you two only ever have room in your heads for one idea—surpassing gods, becoming immortal, that sort of thing. Typical.”
“Don’t act like you’ve seen through everything!”
“I’ll finish you off while you’re riding high and prove that I’m the strongest!”
Ark let out a scornful “Hah!”

“You lot, and everyone like you who forgets about death, all throw away without hesitation the precious thing you were born with from the very start… never once imagining there are those who desperately crave it… that’s exactly why it makes me sick.”
“What are you even talking about!? Explain it properly!”

“You never properly explain yourselves to others. And yet you have the nerve to demand explanations from your opponent—don’t you think that’s selfish? How many times is this exchange going to repeat… hah.”
“They’re the wonderful, rotten guests conveniently shipped in as other-world raiders by those posing as gods!”
I realized Hou-kun had just delivered a witty little joke there. Ark turned a subzero glare on Hou-kun.
“Considering the bird is one of the very causes that caused me so much trouble, that attitude of yours is quite something, isn’t it…?”
“I won’t deny that she and I pushed it onto you, but that’s a separate matter from this, isn’t it?”
It seemed Ark was pressing Hou-kun over some old grudge from the past, indeed.
“H-Hou-kun did nothing wrong, I say! If someone must be punished, let it be me, indeed!”
“Motoyasu-kun, you’re defending me without even understanding what this is about! It’s no joking matter, so please stop.”
Ark blinked in surprise, and Hou-kun, remembering me, stepped in to stop me.
“Motoyasu-kun, defending the bird, huh. How kind. Reassuring to know you’re nothing at all like them.”
“I—I’m not such a fine being as that, I say.”

It was true… when I first came to this world, I too had gotten carried away. I’d thought I would save the world and this time build a joyous harem with everyone and live happily. So in the truest sense, perhaps I had no right to condemn the reincarnators the way Hou-kun and the others did.
“What is the difference between me and them, I wonder? Ark, Hou-kun. I’d like you to tell me, indeed.”

I understood that they were terrible people who had to be dealt with no matter what—but there were times I honestly couldn’t tell the difference between us. Weren’t they simply the ones who had achieved, exactly as it was, the very ambition I myself had harbored when I first arrived in this world?

“You’re fundamentally different from them from the start, but… if we’re talking surface level, what sets you apart is that you can get angry out of empathy for someone else’s pain, rather than always putting yourself first.”

“What’s big with these rotten types is that, at their core, it’s always ‘me first,’ never anyone else. Lazy, rotten at the root, yet starving like some kind of hungry demon underneath—that’s what makes them hopeless. Like some creep sending bodily fluids to their favorite idol. As if the idol would ever be happy about that. Disgusting.”

“Unless you make them suffer in hell and force them to truly recognize what they’ve done before burning them, not even the flames of purgatory could make scum like that repent. They really are the world’s garbage.”
Ark and Hou-kun answered my question together. There wasn’t the slightest trace of displeasure on either of their faces.
“Trying to save Raphtalia-chan, a slave, from Naofumi-kun—that was a noble feeling. It’s just that, for various reasons, the gears never quite meshed.”
“But because of that, I ended up hurting Father, indeed.”
It was true that I had been shallow, and without properly investigating anything, I had challenged Father to a duel.
“Naofumi-kun doesn’t hold that much of a grudge over what you did, you know. The real culprit is the true mastermind.”
Even Ark said it was the Crimson Swine, who had used me to the fullest, that was to blame. But that wasn’t good enough, indeed. My sin was that I had trusted the wrong person.
